bole.text: Straight cylindrical bole 75-115 cm diameter (Useful Tropical Plants). Branching mainly near the top; Spanish Wikipedia mentions 'gambas' (buttresses). English Wikipedia: latex is tapped from the buttresses in the Golfo Dulce forest. Titi Conservation Alliance (src 3): 'large well developed roots' supporting the tree, trunk up to 1.5 m.

crown.text: Climax species that dominates canopies on well-drained slopes (English Wikipedia).

phenology.flower_colour: cream or yellowish (small globular flower heads)
phenology.fruit: round, juicy, fleshy fruit up to 5 cm diameter with edible seeds

bark.colour: grey, with irregular whitish horizontal patches
bark.text: Greyish bark with irregular whitish horizontal patches (Spanish Wikipedia, src 1); grey and thick, exuding white sticky latex when cut (src 3). The fibrous bark was used for cloth and sails (UTP, en Wikipedia).

habitat.range: Costa Rica (central and south Pacific, including Osa) and Panama to Colombia, Venezuela, Ecuador, Peru, Bolivia, the Guianas and the Amazon basin.

notes: Height: Spanish Wikipedia up to 50 m; Titi Conservation Alliance up to 40 m; English Wikipedia and Useful Tropical Plants 30 m. typical [30,40] spans those maxima, not a measured typical. Leaves: simple, alternate, large, with a very acute apex; hairy stipules enclose the developing leaves (es Wikipedia, src 3); no sizes or colours found. Phenology is from the Titi Conservation Alliance (central and south Pacific Costa Rica, Quepos to Osa): flowers all year, fruit mainly April-June. Flower colour: cream or yellowish (es Wikipedia); small and white (src 3). Fruit size 'up to 5 cm' from es Wikipedia, which also says many species eat the fruit avidly without naming them. Evergreen per Useful Tropical Plants ('Evergreen forest formations below 400 m'). Shade-tolerant per English Wikipedia. Src 3 names 'sainos' and 'chanchos de monte'; the scientific names are my mapping of those Costa Rican names (collared and white-lipped peccary). Domestic animals: cattle eat leaves and branch tips, pigs the fruit (en Wikipedia), not listed. No Corcovado-specific fauna records found. Costa Rican trees are subsp. occidentale per HVAA image captions (not verified in a treatment). Flora Costaricensis and the Golfo Dulce field guide (Stapfia 78) were blocked (403).
